headline: High-risk write-capable marketing agent paired with a read-only collection agent creates default data-flow and conflict risks; prompt-injection risk is limited by the read-only side.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest B directly. Agent B has file and API surfaces plus shared-context skills, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or parser bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or file handoff, which is unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies B output into A-facing instructions or files
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Disable copy-paste handoff between agents during review
Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Add a short human-authored delimiter before any transferred text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, while B touches marketing content and can read/write files with allowlisted egress. There is no evidence of shared workspace or sensitive data classes, so leakage is limited to accidental exposure of marketing context through manual transfer or shared files if configured.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF marketing context files are copied from B into A-visible storage
mitigations: Store A and B artifacts in separate directories
Remove sensitive marketing notes before transfer
Restrict B's allowlisted egress to approved domains only
Audit shared files for unintended context spill

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or subprocess capability, but B can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and run multiple instances. If both are aimed at the same directory, B can overwrite or race with artifacts while A cannot coordinate or lock. The conflict is one-sided but real in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF A and B are configured to share a writable directory
IF multiple B instances operate on the same files without external locking
mitigations: Assign B a unique working directory
Run only one B instance per workspace
Use file locks for shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a collection source and B's sandboxing says skills reference each other and build on shared context, so B may treat upstream content as authoritative. Because A is non-runnable and cannot verify B's actions, the main risk is B propagating unverified marketing claims or instructions into downstream outputs.
conditions: IF B consumes A-derived text as shared context
IF B renders or acts on A-derived claims without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review before B publishes outputs
Add a verification checklist for claims sourced from A
Mark A-derived text as untrusted input
requires-engineering: insert a validation stage between A and B

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is identified for A, and B only touches marketing content and product marketing context. The profiles do not show residency, certification, retention, or PHI handling mismatches, so a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced. A is not cited separately because it has no relevant compliance surface.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
IF retention or residency requirements are added to B's workflow
mitigations: Document data-class boundaries for both agents
Keep regulated data out of this pair
